project_tracker_diagnostic: Tall herbaceous white composite with opposite serrate leaves and flat-topped clusters of fuzzy white heads; more herbaceous and rank than shrubby boneset.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common or useful Central Texas fall/white composite for field learning.

morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite, coarsely serrate, petiolate, often with scattered glands.
morphology_keys.heads: Small white discoid heads in broad corymbs/panicles.
morphology_keys.reproductive_confirmation: FNA: 9–15 disk florets per capitulum; 8–12 phyllaries in 1–2 series, usually 1–3 mm, compared with genus-specific Ageratina and Chromolaena architecture.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.

look_here_first: Differentiate late boneset from white mistflower/white snakeroot by its tall branched HERBACEOUS form, narrower opposite lanceolate gland-dotted leaves (usually 20–90+ × 5–40 mm), and 9–15 florets per capitulum. FNA describes 8–12 phyllaries in 1–2 series, each usually 1–3 mm long.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Versus A. havanensis: herbaceous and tall vs woody evergreen shrub. Versus A. altissima: leaves narrower and more lanceolate, with gland-dots, and often stronger distal branching; inspect individual heads and phyllaries. Versus C. odorata: short 1–3 mm Eupatorium phyllaries in 1–2 series and generally much shorter involucres, instead of cylindrical 8–10 mm involucres with 4–6+ phyllary series.

diagnostic_photo_requirements.must_show: 8–12 phyllaries in 1–2 series; head with 9–15 florets
